NoteTexAccessor::macro_use¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::macro_use() const

Build A Per-Cell Control-Word Vocabulary¶

macro_use() extracts the distinct TeX control words encountered in each Text cell. Tokens retain their leading backslash. A following star is retained too, so \section* and \section remain distinguishable authored forms. The first occurrence determines order, and later occurrences of the same complete lexeme in that cell are suppressed.

Deduplication is deliberately per cell, not global. If \beta appears in two cells, each cell owns a \beta token. That contract lets callers compare lane vocabularies without reconstructing ownership. Use command_names when every occurrence is needed and the leading backslash/star are not wanted.

This is a lexical vocabulary, not a macro-call graph. Built-in commands, user-defined commands, declaration words, and command names inside arguments are all control words and may be reported. The extractor does not establish whether a command is defined, reachable, or executed. Control symbols such as \% are not control words and are omitted. A doubled backslash is skipped as an escaped pair rather than misread as a command start.

tokens() is a flat Text Note and offsets() is an Int64 Note. Cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]); receiver shape is represented by row-major lane order and these boundaries. Undefined input returns undefined tokens with the canonical offsets [0], while defined non-Text input is rejected.

The scanner is linear in source bytes. It maintains a per-cell hash set for first-seen deduplication and copies each retained lexeme once. Consequently, memory is proportional to the number and total bytes of distinct control words in each cell, not the number of occurrences.

Example 1: First-Seen Deduplication And Starred Forms¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\alpha \beta \alpha \\gamma \section* \section)",
    R"(\beta \delta \beta)"});
const auto result = source.tex().macro_use();

std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["\\alpha", "\\beta", "\\section*", "\\section", "\\beta", "\\delta"]

The repeated \alpha is removed from the first cell, but \section* does not collapse into \section. The escaped \\gamma is absent. \beta appears again because the second cell has its own vocabulary.

Example 2: Inspect The Per-Cell Ranges¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 4, 6]

The first lane owns four distinct lexemes; the second owns two.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().macro_use();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().macro_use();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "macro use Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
macro use Int64: rejected
